target.title: fix(cron): keep valid env vars when a sibling env value is non-string
target.body:
Closes #105433

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users creating or updating a cron command job with `env` that includes any non-string value (for example `env: { FOO: "bar", DEBUG: true }`) would silently lose the entire `env` block during payload normalization, including the valid string entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron payload normalization now drops only invalid env keys/values and keeps the remaining string entries, matching the existing command payload SQLite codec filter behavior. If no valid entries remain, `env` is still removed.

## User Impact

Command cron jobs keep their valid environment variables when one sibling value is the wrong type, instead of wiping the whole `env` map.

## Evidence

- Focused tests in `src/cron/normalize.test.ts` cover mixed valid/invalid env and all-invalid env.
- Local proof (Testbox/Crabbox binary unavailable in this environment): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/normalize.test.ts` → 62 passed.
